finding.claim: Stored SSRF via webhook callback URL. subscribe() stores a caller-supplied callbackUrl with no validation. notifyAll() later POSTs the payload to every stored URL from the server's network position. An attacker can subscribe with http://169.254.169.254/..., http://localhost:<port>/..., or an internal service URL. The server then makes the request every minute. The scheme, host and resolved IP are unchecked, so any http/https destination is reachable, including cloud metadata and internal admin endpoints. Impact is mainly blind SSRF with an attacker-influenced POST body. The response is discarded, so it is not directly readable. The request is deferred and repeated.
finding.source: callbackUrl parameter of subscribe(), from the POST /subscribe body (Jobs.java:13)

trace.note: stored unvalidated in the static subscriptions map
notifyAll() iterates subscriptions.values() on the once-per-minute job
URI.create(cb) builds the request URI with no scheme, host or IP check
client.send() issues the POST to the attacker-chosen destination

finding.guards_checked: No scheme allowlist, host allowlist, DNS resolution or private-IP check, and no authentication or authorization in this file. The default java.net.http.HttpClient does not follow redirects, which is not a defense here because the initial URL is already attacker-chosen. The response body is discarded, so exploitation is blind, but a side-effecting POST to internal services is still possible.

verdict.reason: src/Jobs.java:13-14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated and src/Jobs.java:21-24 builds URI.create(cb) and calls client.send() with no scheme, host or IP check. The only regex guard in the file is on thumb() at line 30, a separate path. The finding's note that the POST body is attacker-influenced is unverified, since the payload comes from the notifyAll caller, but the destination is attacker-chosen.
